name: Seele
summary: AI game-studio agent that turns a text prompt, image or drawing into a playable 2D or 3D game in the browser, with Three.js, Unity and Unreal targets and generated 3D assets, images, video and audio, billed in Koin credits.
best_for: hobbyists, students and teachers who want to turn an idea, a drawing or a photo into a playable browser game without writing code, and indie developers who want to prototype a game idea quickly before building it properly
skip_if: you plan to sell or monetise the game on the $20 plan, because commercial use starts at Pro; or you need a fixed budget per project, because Koin costs are only known after the work; or you need guaranteed access to the source code, because the help centre says code download is not currently available
honest_knock:
You cannot know in advance what a game will cost. Koins are deducted by the AI time, cloud time and third-party tools a task uses, and the help centre says every change you ask for, from renaming a character to fixing a bug, is a new generation that costs Koins again. It also says Unity projects cost significantly more than lightweight Three.js web games. The 360 free Koins are meant for a first build, and one public review we read, from a 16-year-old, says he ran out before finishing his first game.

The cheapest plan does not let you sell what you make. Commercial use is listed on Pro and Ultra only, and the terms (section 4.2, updated 28 July 2026) say the right to publish, sell or advertise in your games comes with an active subscription at Pro or above, which is $50 a month or $39 billed annually. On Standard at $20 you can build and share, not earn.

The pricing page and the terms disagree on the two things that protect your money. The upgrade page FAQ says unused Koins roll over and the help centre says they never expire, while the terms say unused subscription Koins do not carry over to the next billing period. The upgrade page advertises a 7-day free trial and a 7-day money-back guarantee, while the terms say all payments are final and non-refundable, and that refunds may be refused for anything bought with a coupon or discount, which covers the 50% first-month offer the page applies by default. The terms also say a chargeback raised without first emailing support will be treated as fraud. Finally, the homepage promises you can take your Unity project with you, while the help centre's article on Koins says source code download is currently not available. We have not used the product.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-02 on seeles.ai/upgrade on the monthly, annual and Koin Pack tabs, on the workspace sign-up screen and in the help centre) Everything is paid for in Koins, the platform's credit, deducted per task according to the model, cloud time and third-party tools used, so there is no fixed price per game. A new account gets 360 Koins on sign-up, with no credit card. Standard is $20 a month for 2,000 Koins, Pro $50 for 6,000 and Ultra $200 for 25,000; billed annually they show as $17, $39 and $167 a month. The toggle says annual saves 22%, which is true for Pro; on Standard it is 15% and on Ultra about 16%. Pro adds commercial use, 'advanced monetization', 20 instead of 10 parallel tasks and 50GB instead of 20GB of storage; Ultra adds 200GB, a private cloud host and publishing support. Koin Packs without a plan cost $20 for 2,000, $50 for 5,000, $200 for 20,000 and $500 for 50,000, and do not include plan benefits such as the advanced models, asset downloads or the priority queue. The upgrade page applied a 'New User 50% Off First Month' coupon by default. Payment by card through Stripe. The terms name SEELE AI, Inc. and the usage policy SEELE Technology Limited.

compare_with.name: Rosebud AI
compare_with.why: Rosebud AI is the closest alternative: it also turns prompts into browser games and charges in credits. On its pricing page, read on 2 October 2026, Indie Dev is $15 a month, 10x Dev at $30 adds full commercial rights and removes Rosebud branding, Pro at $50 adds downloadable project code and Scale is $100; Rosebud says unused credits roll over once and then expire. So on Rosebud commercial rights cost $30 a month and code download is a listed feature at $50, while on Seele commercial use starts at $50 and code download is not available according to its own help centre. Seele's case is breadth: Unity and Unreal targets, 3D assets, video and audio generation in the same workspace. Pick Rosebud if you want to own and sell a web game at the lowest price; pick Seele if you want a 3D or Unity project and a single tool for the game and its assets.
